topic: Assess rooftop solar installation trends in Northstar.

snippets.text: In 2025, the fictional Northstar region installed 120 megawatts of rooftop solar, up from 100 megawatts in 2024. Installations are measured as new capacity, not electricity generated.
Northstar's residential rooftop solar installations increased from 40 to 55 megawatts between 2024 and 2025. Commercial installations increased from 60 to 65 megawatts over the same period.
Solara reduced the average installed price of its home battery from 8,000 credits in 2024 to 7,600 credits in 2025. These prices exclude maintenance.

draft_memo.title: Rooftop Solar Installation Trends in Northstar
draft_memo.body:
In 2025, the Northstar region installed a total of 120 megawatts of rooftop solar capacity, an increase from 100 megawatts in 2024, representing a growth of 20 megawatts over the one-year period [P01]. This increase in installations is measured as new capacity rather than the amount of electricity generated, which is a critical distinction in understanding the data [P01]. Within this total, residential rooftop solar installations rose from 40 megawatts in 2024 to 55 megawatts in 2025, marking an increase of 15 megawatts [P02]. Concurrently, commercial rooftop solar installations also saw growth, rising from 60 megawatts in 2024 to 65 megawatts in 2025, which is an increase of 5 megawatts [P02]. 

The average installed price of home batteries in Northstar, provided by Solara, decreased from 8,000 credits in 2024 to 7,600 credits in 2025, a reduction of 400 credits [P04]. It is important to note that these prices do not include maintenance costs, which can affect the overall investment in solar technology [P04]. The data presented covers only the years 2024 and 2025 and does not provide insights into trends prior to 2024 or future projections beyond 2025, as stated in the source [P01]. Additionally, the figures represent installed capacity and pricing but do not account for the operational efficiency or actual electricity generation from the installed systems, which is a limitation of the data [P01]. The data is fictional and should be interpreted within that context, limiting its applicability to real-world scenarios [P01]. The measurement of installations as new capacity rather than electricity generated is crucial for understanding the growth dynamics in the solar sector in Northstar [P01].
footnotes: [P01] In 2025, Northstar installed 120 megawatts of rooftop solar, up from 100 megawatts in 2024. Installations are measured as new capacity, not electricity generated.
[P02] Northstar's residential rooftop solar installations increased from 40 to 55 megawatts between 2024 and 2025. Commercial installations increased from 60 to 65 megawatts over the same period.
[P04] Solara reduced the average installed price of its home battery from 8,000 credits in 2024 to 7,600 credits in 2025. These prices exclude maintenance.
